claims.text: A high-fiber diet lowers mean daily preprandial plasma glucose concentrations compared to an ADA-recommended moderate-fiber diet in patients with type 2 diabetes.
A high-fiber diet decreases daily urinary glucose excretion in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to a moderate-fiber diet.
A high-fiber diet lowers the area under the curve for 24-hour plasma glucose concentrations by 10 percent in patients with type 2 diabetes.
A high-fiber diet lowers the area under the curve for 24-hour insulin concentrations by 12 percent in patients with type 2 diabetes.
A high-fiber diet reduces plasma total cholesterol concentrations by 6.7 percent in patients with type 2 diabetes.
A high-fiber diet reduces triglyceride concentrations by 10.2 percent in patients with type 2 diabetes.
A high-fiber diet reduces very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations by 12.5 percent in patients with type 2 diabetes.

evidence.description: During the sixth week, mean daily preprandial plasma glucose concentrations were 13 mg per deciliter lower (95 percent confidence interval, 1 to 24 mg per deciliter; P=0.04) on the high-fiber diet compared to the ADA diet.
Daily urinary glucose excretion mean median difference was 1.3 g (0.23; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.03 to 1.83 g; P=0.008) lower on the high-fiber diet.
The high-fiber diet lowered the area under the curve for 24-hour plasma glucose concentrations by 10 percent (P=0.02).
The high-fiber diet lowered the area under the curve for 24-hour insulin concentrations by 12 percent (P=0.05).
The high-fiber diet reduced plasma total cholesterol concentrations by 6.7 percent (P=0.02).
The high-fiber diet reduced triglyceride concentrations by 10.2 percent (P=0.02).
The high-fiber diet reduced very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations by 12.5 percent (P=0.01).

methodologies.name: Randomized Crossover Dietary Trial
methodologies.description: A randomized crossover study comparing six weeks of an ADA moderate-fiber diet (24 g total fiber) against six weeks of an unfortified high-fiber diet (50 g total fiber) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
conditions: Two 6-week intervention periods in a randomized crossover design
Diets prepared in a research kitchen with identical macronutrient and energy content
Moderate-fiber diet (24 g total: 8 g soluble, 16 g insoluble)
High-fiber diet (50 g total: 25 g soluble, 25 g insoluble)

limitations.text: The effect of increasing the intake of dietary fiber on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus is controversial in existing literature.
The study intervention was evaluated on a small sample size of 13 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus over six-week period durations.
